# Visual grammar

Choose the smallest structure that makes the idea undeniable.

| Mode | Use when the script expresses | Composition rules |
|---|---|---|
| `single-scene` | one concrete situation, atmosphere, or example | One environment and focal action. No diagram scaffolding unless essential. |
| `metaphor` | an abstract claim or capability | One surprising physical analogy. Keep the mapping obvious and avoid multiple metaphors. |
| `contrast` | cheap vs expensive, before vs after, wrong vs right | Two balanced halves, one center divider, repeated subject, visibly different outcome. |
| `flow-3` | a short causal chain or three-stage process | Three large nodes left to right, one continuous arrow, numbered circles only if order matters. |
| `pipeline-4` | production workflow with four or five operations | Evenly spaced stages with distinct silhouettes. Labels beneath nodes. Avoid UI-card clutter. |
| `journey` | current state, transformation, desired end state | A continuous path through spatially distinct zones. Put the CTA or destination at the end. |
| `system-map` | many inputs held or coordinated by one system | One center hub with clear incoming and outgoing relationships. Maximum five satellites. |
| `collection` | libraries, references, choices, or examples | Organized shelf, pinboard, or grid with one highlighted selection. Do not use random floating cards. |
| `hierarchy` | levels, priorities, or build-up | Staircase, stack, mountain, or nested containers. Make direction and rank unmistakable. |
| `loop` | recurring publishing, feedback, or automated cycle | Three or four stages around a circular arrow with a clearly marked entry or benefit. |
| `device-sync` | phone, desktop, remote access, or publishing | Show one shared artifact across devices with directional sync lines, not cloned unrelated screens. |
| `checklist` | a short set of requirements | One main object surrounded by 3–5 large check marks and icons. Use labels only when icons are ambiguous. |

## Arrow rules

- Use arrows only for motion, causality, sequence, transformation, or selection.
- Begin and end every arrow at a specific object.
- Use one arrow style per frame.
- Pink arrows indicate the main intended action; gray arrows may show secondary context.
- Avoid crossing arrows. Rearrange the composition instead.
- A flow should still read correctly if all labels are hidden.

## Layout rules

- Reserve the top 15–20% for the title.
- Put the visual claim in the central 65%.
- Keep the outer 7% clear for safe cropping.
- Use one dominant object at roughly twice the area of secondary objects.
- Prefer left-to-right reading. Use top-to-bottom only for hierarchy.
- Use circles or underlines to emphasize one moment, not every object.

## Choosing between similar modes

- Use `contrast` when two states are the point; use `journey` when movement between states is the point.
- Use `flow-3` when the steps are concepts; use `single-scene` when the same action can be shown naturally in one place.
- Use `system-map` when relationships are simultaneous; use `pipeline-4` when they happen in order.
- Use `collection` for options; use `checklist` for requirements.
